hero.text: I have been writing code since {since}, in technical leadership and coaching roles at Sony, eBay/GittiGidiyor, ACM and iyzico. Today I build Craftgate, a payment orchestration platform, as its Chief Software Crafter. I founded the Software Craftsmanship Turkey community in {founded}, and I talk about how good software gets made: craftsmanship, team culture, and what is still worth keeping now that code is cheap to generate.

game.heading: Git is a graph
game.intro: In 2016 I gave a talk in Turkish, {talk}. Its one idea: every git command is a move on a graph. Commits are nodes; branches, tags and HEAD are pointers to them. Here you run real git commands, typed or tapped together, and move commits and pointers until your graph matches the goal. Each level is a piece of my own history, and solving it tells you a little more about me.

levels.title: Hello, 2001
levels.story: Summer 2001: my first job, as a software engineer at TÜSSİDE. A year later I was a lab assistant at Marmara University.
levels.task: Make two commits on main. Watch what the main pointer does.
levels.hint: Type git commit. A commit is a new node in the graph, and the branch you are on moves to it.

fact.text: My first job was in the summer of 2001, as a software engineer at TÜSSİDE. I have been writing code ever since.

levels.title: Pointers, not copies
levels.story: In 2004 I joined Sony, where I spent most of the following decade.
levels.task: Create a branch called sony, switch to it, and commit on it. main must stay where it is.
levels.hint: A branch is only a pointer to a commit. git checkout -b <name> creates one and moves HEAD onto it.

fact.text: I joined Sony in 2004 and stayed for most of the following decade, from software engineer to Scrum Master, technical lead, solution architect and agile practice lead.

levels.title: I left twice
levels.story: I left Sony twice and came back both times. My career page draws those detours as side branches.
levels.task: Merge air-force back into main so the detour stays visible. A fast-forward would hide it.
levels.hint: When main has not moved since the branch started, git merge only slides main forward. --no-ff forces a merge commit with two parents.

fact.text: From 2006 to 2007 I served as a software officer in the Turkish Air Force, and in 2012 I spent six months at GittiGidiyor, eBay's marketplace in Türkiye. Both times I came back to Sony.

levels.title: Launch day
levels.story: Craftgate grew inside Craftbase, the company we started in 2018, and was introduced publicly in January 2021.
levels.task: Tag the commit "Public launch" as launch. Do not move any branch.
levels.hint: A tag is a pointer that never moves. git tag <name> <commit> puts one anywhere, and HEAD~1 means one commit before HEAD.

fact.text: In April 2018 I co-founded Craftbase with Hakan Erdoğan, Sabri Onur Tüzün and Murathan Özcan. Craftgate grew inside it and was introduced publicly in January 2021.

levels.title: Forgot something
levels.story: Everyone commits and then notices something is missing. The commit you are about to fix holds the slides of a talk.
levels.task: Fix the last commit instead of adding a new one.
levels.hint: git commit --amend makes a new commit on the same parent and moves the branch to it. The old commit is still there, only unreachable.

fact.text: In 2016 I gave a talk in Turkish at Karabük University's Programming Days: "Git: Bildiğiniz Gibi Değil", Git is not what you think. This game is built on its idea: every Git command is a move on a graph.

levels.title: Straight lines
levels.story: A small typofix branch waits while main moves on. Rebase replays it on top, so history reads as one straight line.
levels.task: Move typofix on top of main without a merge commit.
levels.hint: git rebase <upstream> copies your branch's commits onto the tip of upstream and moves the branch there. The originals become unreachable.

fact.text: I have taken Git talks across Europe: Git Anti-Patterns at Devoxx Poland and XP Days Ukraine in 2017, and 10 Git Anti-Patterns You Should Be Aware Of at GrowIT in Serbia in 2018.

levels.title: Only what is tested
levels.story: In 2022 I wrote down the foundations of Craftgate's team culture. One line of it: untested development is incomplete development.
levels.task: Bring only the two tested commits from experiments onto main, in their original order.
levels.hint: git cherry-pick copies commits onto where you stand. Name several and they are applied in the order you give them.

fact.text: In 2022 I wrote down the foundations of Craftgate's team culture. Among them: no seniority levels in job titles, no team leader position, and untested development is incomplete development.

levels.title: We pursued neither
levels.story: By September 2021 eleven investors had reached out to Craftgate and three large companies wanted to buy it. We pursued neither.
levels.task: Move main back two commits, as if those calls never happened. Nobody else has seen them yet.
levels.hint: git reset moves the branch you are on to another commit. The commits it leaves behind are not deleted, only unreachable.

fact.text: Instead of investors or buyers, we chose to leave our profitable service work. Since 1 January 2022 the company has been only Craftgate.

levels.title: Undo in public
levels.story: On 28 November 2017 I asked Apple on Twitter whether it knew that anyone could log in as root on macOS High Sierra with an empty password. The fix shipped the next day.
levels.task: main is public. Undo the commit "Credential check" without rewriting history.
levels.hint: git revert adds a new commit that undoes an old one. Nothing is rewritten, so everyone who already has main stays in step.

fact.text: The root bug was not my find: the infrastructure team at the company I worked for came across it and reported it to Apple five days earlier. My tweet was covered around the world, and Apple released Security Update 2017-001 on 29 November 2017.

levels.title: Nothing is lost
levels.story: I founded Software Craftsmanship Turkey in 2014. Someone has just deleted its branch with git branch -D.
levels.task: Bring the branch scturkey back exactly where it was, and stay on main. git reflog remembers where HEAD has been.
levels.hint: The commits are still there, faded. Find the hash of the newest one in git reflog, then git branch scturkey <hash>.

fact.text: Software Craftsmanship Turkey has run more than 200 free meetups since I founded it in 2014, and I have facilitated code retreats since 2013, including the Global Day of Coderetreat.

levels.title: Burning the ships
levels.story: Craftgate grew on top of Craftbase's client work. At the end of 2021 we left all of that service work behind.
levels.task: Move craftgate's own two commits off services and directly onto main. Leave services where it is.
levels.hint: git rebase --onto <new base> <old base> <branch> takes the commits after old base and replays them on new base.

fact.text: Since leaving service work, Craftgate has raised investment, made the Deloitte Technology Fast 50 Türkiye, and opened its first market abroad, in Spain.

levels.title: Ship the talk
levels.story: I have given more than 200 seminars at companies and universities, and spoken at conferences across Europe and the Middle East. Time to ship one more talk.
levels.task: Put talk on top of main, merge it into main with a merge commit, tag that merge devoxx, and delete the talk branch.
levels.hint: One move at a time: rebase, go back to main, merge with --no-ff, tag, then delete the branch. git branch -d refuses to delete what is not merged.

fact.text: Outside Türkiye I have spoken at Devoxx in Belgium, Poland and Ukraine, XP Days Ukraine, GrowIT in Serbia, ITAKE in Romania, Agile Tour Kaunas, Bosnia Agile Day and Agile Middle East in Dubai.
